title: Add KMS usage provenance attestor and ephemeral RBAC delegation proxy
author: Amira Chen
release_notes: Adds CMK origin attestation middleware, ephemeral RBAC delegation proxy for short-lived cross-region KMS requests, and audit enrichment for KMS usage provenance. Backwards-compatible server-side change; customers do not need config changes but operators should rollout the new helm chart values for private deployments.
description:
Motivation: We need stronger proof that a CMK call originated from an expected region/service identity and better attribution for compliance audits. Existing region-pin checks are static and do not cover transient delegation flows that happen when we route requests to fallback KMS providers. This PR introduces a lightweight provenance attestor that validates a signed CMK-origin header from KMS proxy hops and a companion ephemeral RBAC delegation proxy that issues short-lived session tokens for cross-region KMS calls.

What this PR does: Adds a provenance attestor middleware (serving/kms) that validates an origin signature and resolves a provenance assertion into an internal claim used by RBAC checks. Adds a session-scoped delegation layer (serving/rbac) which mints ephemeral delegation tokens with limited scope and explicit region affinity. Adds audit enrichment that records provenance claim, delegation token id, and resolved service principal in KMS audit events (internal/audit). Adds operator-facing helm values to enable/disable the delegation proxy and tune TTLs.

High level files changed: provenance attestor implementation, delegation proxy, RBAC policy shim to accept session-scoped tokens, audit enricher, integration tests, e2e scenario harness updates, and helm values.

Security considerations: provenance attestor verifies a signed header (HMAC over canonical request + origin metadata) using a rotating attestation key stored in the platform KMS; the delegation proxy requires the caller to present a valid tenant-scoped service identity and enforces scope minimization. We added additional rate limiting on the delegation endpoint to mitigate abuse. All new secrets are wired into KMS + KMS-secret-provider and no plaintext secret is checked-in.

Migration / rollout plan: feature is behind a runtime flag (env REDWOOD_KMS_PROVENANCE=off by default). Gradual rollout steps: enable attestor in canary region, run integration traffic with internal test tenants, switch on delegation proxy with conservative TTL (60s), monitor audit logs and RBAC denials. For Redwood Private customers, helm values/deployment notes included in charts/values-private.yaml.

Testing: unit tests for attestor and delegation token lifecycle; integration tests exercising cross-region fallback path and ensuring provenance is recorded in audit events; manual QA scenario that replays an incident (replay id ENG-9042) to validate that audit records match expected provenance claims. CI run had one flaky integration test (kms_fallback_integration_test) which was rerun and passed.

Risks and mitigations: risk of false negatives if attestation key rotation is misaligned with proxies; mitigated by key version check and a short grace window. Performance impact: added a small crypto HMAC check per routed KMS request; measured +0.8ms median tail in canary, within SLO for most tenants.

Related: ENG-9042 (design doc), SEC-121 (compliance review), SUP-345 (customer support thread about missing KMS provenance in audit logs).
